option.approach: Investigate whether a projection dilation of the positive increments can be constructed in an AW*-amplification that preserves the original algebra as a corner. If projection joins survive compression, use that to construct the supremum.

options.approach: Audit the monotone sequential completeness claim independently of the quasitrace. Identify whether a valid theorem requires additional normality or completeness assumptions absent from the problem.

options.counterfactual: A bounded increasing sequence in a finite AW*-factor can have a least upper bound while all its positive increments have the same strictly positive quasitrace.
options.approach: Separate the constant-increment condition from the absence-of-supremum condition. Determine which order-continuity property of the quasitrace fails when a supremum exists but the increments do not decay.

options.counterfactual: A bounded increasing sequence in a finite AW*-factor can have a least upper bound while all its positive increments have the same strictly positive quasitrace.
options.approach: Study the decreasing positive remainders obtained by subtracting the sequence from its supremum. Their greatest lower bound is zero, so they provide a direct test of quasitracial continuity from above.

options.counterfactual: A bounded increasing sequence in a finite AW*-factor can have a least upper bound while all its positive increments have the same strictly positive quasitrace.
options.approach: Examine whether a sequence with a supremum can be transferred to a different finite AW*-factor or corner so that its increments are preserved but its supremum is lost. Any construction would need an explicit argument identifying the new upper-bound set.
